classification.difficultyReason: Construct the square and midpoints, use SAS to prove equal segments, then SSS to prove equal angles.

content.prompt: $PRSV$ is a square. The midpoint of $PV$ is $X$ and $T$ is the midpoint of $SV$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw a diagram and prove that $RX=RT$.

answer.short: $PR=RS$, $PX=ST$ and $\angle RPX=\angle RST=90^\circ$. Hence $\triangle RPX\equiv\triangle RST$ (SAS), so $RX=RT$.
answer.worked:
Draw square $PRSV$, mark midpoint $X$ on $PV$ and midpoint $T$ on $SV$, and join $RX$ and $RT$.

In $\triangle RPX$ and $\triangle RST$:

$PR=RS$ (sides of a square),

$PX=ST$ (halves of the equal sides $PV$ and $SV$),

$\angle RPX=\angle RST=90^\circ$ (angles of a square).

Therefore $\triangle RPX\equiv\triangle RST$ (SAS).

Hence $RX=RT$ (matching sides of congruent triangles).

spec.description: Completed square construction with the two midpoints and required segments RX and RT.
spec.mathematics: P,R,S,V occur cyclically; X is the midpoint of PV and T the midpoint of SV.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; the source supplies no question diagram.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Join $RV$ and prove that $\angle TRV=\angle XRV$.

answer.short: $RX=RT$, $VX=VT$ and $RV$ is common. Thus $\triangle RXV\equiv\triangle RTV$ (SSS), so $\angle TRV=\angle XRV$.
answer.worked:
Join $RV$.

In $\triangle RXV$ and $\triangle RTV$:

$RX=RT$ (part a),

$VX=VT$ (halves of the equal sides $PV$ and $SV$),

$RV=RV$ (common side).

Therefore $\triangle RXV\equiv\triangle RTV$ (SSS).

Hence $\angle TRV=\angle XRV$ (matching angles of congruent triangles).

spec.description: Part a construction completed with diagonal RV, dashed as in the teacher evidence.
spec.mathematics: Triangles RXV and RTV have three matching equal sides.
